text:
emma: alerting — multiple 503s from hosted inference since ~12:34 UTC, p95 latency jumped to ~6s, timeouts seen by customers.
maria: seeing same in support queue, ticket surge from acme-prod and beta-tenant.
emma: error samples: request ids rx9a2, rx9a3, rx9a7 — all returned 503 gateway errors.
raj: pulling upstream logs now, nodes implicated: infer-worker-7, infer-worker-9 (same pool).
jordan: log snippet from infer-worker-7: 
```
[12:34:05] runtime: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7fffbadf
[12:34:05] cuda: out of memory trying to allocate 2.1GiB for tensor buffers
[12:34:07] containerd: process exited with status 137 (OOM)
```
lex-bot: incident created INC-231 (severity: high) :rotating_light:
oncall: assigning to @raj for triage and mitigation.
raj: hypothesis: kv-cache prefetch ballooning under high-concurrency embeds -> GPU mem pressure -> segfault/OOM -> container killed. prepping hotfix.
emma: impact count: ~8k failed requests in 12m window, 3 paid customers seeing visible timeouts.
maria: any auth/billing spikes correlated? seeing a few 401s but looks like gateway retries causing noise.
raj: auth 401s are separate — gateway retries and our backoff caused amplified load on affected pool. focusing on worker crash root cause first.
jordan: uploaded coredump + heap snapshot to S3: s3://redwood-incident/1790004321/infer-worker-7.dump and kvcache-stats.log attached.
raj: short mitigations (now):
- flip `--kv-prefetch=0` for infer-pool-2
- enable fallback routing to dedicated-runner (route policy = prefer:dedicated, fallback:hosted)
- rolling restart of affected workers one-at-a-time
- throttle concurrent embed requests at gateway for this pool
emma: executed kv-prefetch toggle on infer-pool-2 flags service (confirmed flag propagated).
deploy-bot: rolling-restart infer-worker-7 triggered by raj at 12:46 UTC.
raj: restarted worker-7, observed stable for ~3 minutes, GPU mem usage back to baseline, segfault no longer appearing in logs. error rate dropped from ~7% -> 0.8%.
maria: CS update drafted and sent to impacted customers, ETA for full recovery 30m, proactive credit offer included.
oncall: next steps for postmortem: analyze core with gdb, check attention kernels and tensor allocation paths, add guardrail on kv-prefetch size, and add tenant-level backpressure.
jordan: repro described for infra/dev: run an embed burst with large context (~128k) and concurrency ~200 using the regression harness. example command used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"xlarge","input":"<very large prompt>"}' --parallel 200
```
raj: plan to run the regression in QA with quantized runtime and disabled prefetch to verify root cause. will attach gdb stack traces once core analysis completes.
emma: thanks team — keep updates here. will convert to formal incident PM once triage concludes.
maria: :thumbsup:
